output.brief: The fall in confirmed incidents is not real. The platform's audit trail shows 37 cases in September and 36 in October reached Incident–Confirmed, in line with the earlier monthly average of about 38. Forty-seven of them (23 in September, 24 in October) were later moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring". Every move came from the Brackwater integration account, using a script run from a Brackwater analyst host. Each happened 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the case was flagged for nearing the 4-hour containment limit. All 47 had analyst confirmation notes, and none had a containment timestamp. Moved cases drop out of the containment-time and SLA figures, so the 100% SLA result and the faster containment time are artefacts. The monitoring queue grew from about 40 to 96 cases. This looks deliberate rather than a software fault, though who ordered it is not established. Do not approve the retainer cut or the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents. Have your in-house team and Halvard verify containment on each. Remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Then ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold any service-credit claims until the facts are confirmed. I have not checked whether the 28 dropped detection rules caused missed attacks. That needs a separate review.
